item.title: Capture `$?` immediately when you need a command's exit status
item.content: `$?` expands to the exit status of the most recently completed foreground pipeline. Running another command changes what `$?` refers to, so a status that matters should be saved immediately.
item.explanationMarkdown:
If a script needs the status of a particular command, capture it before executing something else:

```bash
grep 'pattern' file.txt
status=$?

printf 'grep exit status: %d\n' "$status"
```

`$?` is not a history of statuses. It is only the status of the most recent relevant command/pipeline.

cards.front: In Bash, what does `$?` contain, and when should you save it?
cards.back: The exit status of the most recently completed foreground pipeline; save it immediately if you need it, before another command overwrites that status.
